# Lesson 3 Reading Quiz — Motors & TRIM
### Fall 2026 · D Block · closes when class starts **Wednesday September 16, 9:50 AM**

> **Fallback copy.** The importable package is `ZUMO_L03_Reading_Quiz_CANVAS_QTI.zip`. If Canvas
> refuses the import, build the quiz by hand from this page — the correct answer is marked **✅**.
> **One attempt, auto-graded, 8 points.** This is a gate, not an exam.

**Why these eight.** Eight sections, eight questions — §1, §3.2, §3.3, §3.5, §3.6, §3.7, §4.2 and §5.5. Nothing here draws on §6–§9: building the TRIM Finder, measuring the number and the challenges are all class work. **Q4 is the one that must not be misremembered** — TRIM adjusts the LEFT motor, in this lesson and every lesson after it. Q8 is the can't-skim question: it asks what `if (trimValue = 5)` actually does, which a student who skimmed will read as a comparison.

---

### 1. You command both motors to speed 200 and the robot curves anyway. According to the lesson, what is going on?
*Source: §1 · bank id `L03_B01` · 1 point*

- **✅ Nothing is broken — no two motors are exactly alike, even from the same factory on the same day**
- One motor is damaged and needs replacing
- The speed command was too high for the battery
- The two motors received different commands

### 2. Every motor value carries two pieces of information. Which is which?
*Source: §3.2 · bank id `L03_B07` · 1 point*

- **✅ The sign is the direction; the size of the number is the speed**
- The sign is the speed; the size is the direction
- The sign is the motor, the size is the speed
- Both are speed — direction is set by a separate command

### 3. The lesson gives your TRIM Finder's driving style a navigator's name. What is it, and what is its flaw?
*Source: §3.3 · bank id `L03_B13` · 1 point*

- **✅ Dead reckoning — estimating position from speed and time, so every small error quietly accumulates and nothing corrects it**
- Dead reckoning — a method so accurate that ships used it to cross oceans
- Triangulation — fixing position from two known landmarks
- Odometry — counting wheel rotations to measure distance

### 4. Why does TRIM always adjust the LEFT motor, even when the right motor is the weak one?
*Source: §3.5 · bank id `L03_B15` · 1 point*

- **✅ So one number means the same thing on every robot and in every later lesson — positive boosts the left, negative eases it down**
- Because the left motor is always the weaker one on a Zumo
- Because the library can only modify the left channel
- Because the left motor is closer to the battery

### 5. Your OLED reads a battery voltage of 4200 mV. What does the lesson tell you to do?
*Source: §3.6 · bank id `L03_B18` · 1 point*

- **✅ Recharge — the cells are empty, and running a pack past empty is what damages it**
- Keep running; this is the normal working plateau
- Nothing — 4200 mV is a fresh reading
- Nothing yet — 4200 mV is the exact voltage at which the cells are damaged, so you are still safe above it

### 6. The lesson warns this is the most common way a TRIM hunt goes backwards. What is it?
*Source: §3.7 · bank id `L03_B22` · 1 point*

- **✅ Judging left and right from your own point of view instead of the robot's, when the robot is driving away from you**
- Testing on tile instead of carpet
- Forgetting to press B before adjusting TRIM
- Using a TRIM_STEP that is too large

### 7. Two robots in the room disagree about how far speed 200 for 2 seconds travels. Before blaming the code, what does the lesson tell you to check?
*Source: §4.2 · bank id `L03_B33` · 1 point*

- **✅ The colored sticker inside the battery compartment, which tells you the gear ratio**
- The TRIM value written on each robot's tape
- Whether both robots are on the same firmware version
- The serial number on the underside of the chassis

### 8. You write if (trimValue = 5) when you meant to compare. What actually happens?
*Source: §5.5 · bank id `L03_B38` · 1 point*

- **✅ trimValue is overwritten with 5, and the block runs every time, because C++ treats the value 5 as true**
- The compiler reports an error and refuses to build
- The block never runs, because assignment is not a comparison
- trimValue is compared to 5 and left unchanged
